data.name: Rehem
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Rehem means 'friend'. In the Bible, this name is used for Rahab the harlot, who risked her own safety to hide and protect the Israelite spies, ultimately saving their lives.

in_greek.name: Ραχήμ

data.cultural_impact: The name "Rehem" holds a rich cultural significance in Jewish history, being the name of a brave and resourceful woman who defied societal norms to help the underdogs. Rahab's actions not only saved the lives of the spies but also her family, and paved the way for the Israelites to conquer the promised land. This name reminds us of the importance of friendship, bravery, and loyalty.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, the name "Rehem" represents God's unwavering love and friendship towards His people. Like Rahab, who risked her life to save the spies, God extends His love and grace, often going against the cultural norms and societal expectations, to provide safety and protection for His children. The name invites us to reflect on God's love and friendship towards us and encourages us to extend that love and kindness to others, regardless of societal norms or expectations.

historical_references.reference: Rehem was a Canaanite city mentioned in the Old Testament book of Joshua. It was one of the cities that the Israelites were instructed to destroy.
historical_references.context: The conquest of Canaan by the Israelites under Joshua's leadership

historical_references.reference: Rehem is also mentioned in the New Testament book of Acts as the site of a miracle performed by the apostle Peter. A man named Aeneas was paralyzed and Peter healed him.
historical_references.context: The spread of Christianity in the Roman Empire
